candidates.evidence: Two sample bands at about 150 and 197 cm-1 with a stronger higher band, the pattern expected for a 1T diselenide. Not verified against reference frequencies: no HfSe2 Raman paper was in the local library and the Valency search failed (token not set), and the skill's reference tables sit outside the folder.
Same 1T diselenide structure class, so a similar two-band pattern is possible. Reference frequencies were not checked; this rests on general structural similarity only.
Has Raman modes in the 130-220 cm-1 region. From memory (unverified) it also has strong bands near 130 and 220 cm-1 that are absent here, which weakens this candidate.
Its main bands are, from memory and unverified, near 110 and 184 cm-1. Both are more than 10 cm-1 from the measured 150 and 197 cm-1, so this is unlikely.

hint_reasoning: The task is an identify task with material_hint null, so there was no stated material to verify. The working folder name contains "HfSe2", but I did not use it as evidence. The ranking rests only on the spectrum.

peaks.source: Strongest sample band. Its A1g-type label rests on D3d selection rules for 1T-type structures (A1g is Raman-active in z(xx)z backscattering along the layer normal). This is general group theory, not a checked reference table. Measured position is 196.7 after the Si offset correction.

Weaker band, area about 0.12 of the 197 cm-1 band (fit areas, measured). The Eg label is an inference from D3d selection rules and is not confirmed. Measured position is 149.6 after the Si offset correction; fit error 0.41 cm-1 before calibration.
Si first-order optical phonon, standard room-temperature value 520.7 cm-1 (general literature value, cited from memory, no locator). Measured offset is +0.42 cm-1.

limits: Only two sample bands were found above the noise (matched-filter SNR above 3 over 60-1100 cm-1). Weak modes below roughly 1000 counts of integrated amplitude could be hidden by the noise (about 280 counts per point).

No reference frequencies were checked. The skill's Computational Raman Database and material notes sit outside the folder, which the task forbids reading. The literature search failed (VALENCY_BOND_TOKEN not set) and the local library has no HfSe2 or ZrSe2 Raman paper. Candidate ranking therefore rests on the band pattern and general structure, not on verified frequencies.
The candidate ranking is not a unique identification. Several layered materials could give two bands near 150 and 197 cm-1.
The spectrum covers only 60-1100 cm-1. Higher-frequency first-order modes and second-order bands were not measured, so they cannot be used to exclude candidates.

Single unpolarized spectrum with no angle series: symmetry labels (A1g, Eg) are inferred from geometry only and cannot be confirmed. The backscattering geometry along the layer normal is stated in metadata but not verified.
Corrected positions after the Si offset (+0.42 cm-1): about 149.6 and 196.7 cm-1, each with about 0.4 cm-1 calibration uncertainty.
Laser at 532 nm, 295 K, and substrate were taken from metadata. No resonance or substrate-interference check was possible.
No layer number, strain, doping, or defect estimate: no applicable relation was available to me, so none was applied.
No cosmic-ray spikes found. The sharp 197 cm-1 feature was checked: it spans about 4 cm-1 with the same width as the Si line, so it is a real band, not a single-point spike.
